verdict.rationale: First-party self-hosting docs say Supermemory runs on your own hardware as the same memory engine behind the hosted platform. It ships as a single self-contained binary with local graph engine, embeddings and LLM, needs no Docker or database provisioning, and pricing lists a self-hosted option. That delivers self-hosting on infrastructure you control, with the binary standing in for the story's example of Docker. Missing for 10: evidence that the self-hosted engine is built from open-source code or that its license allows this, independent or hands-on corroboration of a self-host deployment, and production deployment and operations docs.
